solutions.latex:
The leak each hour is arithmetic with $a = 200$, $d = 50$, and the tank is empty when $S_n = 10\,200$.

Using $S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}\left[2a + (n-1)d\right]$:

$$\begin{aligned} 10\,200 &= \dfrac{n}{2}\left[2(200) + (n-1) \times 50\right] \\ 20\,400 &= n(400 + 50n - 50) \\ 20\,400 &= 350n + 50n^2 \\ n^2 + 7n - 408 &= 0 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} n &= \dfrac{-7 \pm \sqrt{7^2 - 4 \times 1 \times (-408)}}{2} \\ n &= -24 \text{ or } 17 \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Tank empty after 17 hours.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: Correct answer; 2: Obtains $n^2 + 7n - 408 = 0$, or equivalent merit; 1: Correct substitution into $S_n$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The leak each hour is geometric with $a = 200$, $r = \dfrac{250}{200} = 1.25$, $n = 8$.

$$\begin{aligned} S_8 &= \dfrac{200(1.25^8 - 1)}{1.25 - 1} \\ &= 3968.37 \text{ L has leaked out} \end{aligned}$$

$$10\,200 - 3968.37 = 6231.63 \text{ L}$$

$$\dfrac{6231.63}{10\,200} \times 100 = 61.09\%$$

$\therefore$ After 8 hours more than $60\%$ of water remains.

solutions.latex:
15 hours is $x = 1.5$ (tens of hours). A battery still working after 15 hours has $X > 1.5$:

$$\begin{aligned} P(X > 1.5) &= 1 - P(X \le 1.5) = 1 - F(1.5) \\ &= 1 - \dfrac{25}{116}\left(1.5^2 + 3 \times 1.5 - 4\right) \\ &= \dfrac{189}{464} \end{aligned}$$

All three batteries must still be working (independent):

$$\left(\dfrac{189}{464}\right)^3 = 6.76\%$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: Correct answer; 2: Finds $P(X > 1.5) = \dfrac{189}{464}$, or equivalent merit; 1: Uses $1 - F(1.5)$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:

Stationary points where $y' = 0$. By the quotient rule:

$$\begin{aligned} y' &= \dfrac{2x(x - 1)^2 - 2x^2(x - 1)}{(x - 1)^4} \\ &= \dfrac{2x(x - 1)(x - 1 - x)}{(x - 1)^4} \\ &= \dfrac{-2x}{(x - 1)^3} = 0 \end{aligned}$$

So $x = 0$, $y = 0$.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} x & -0.1 & 0 & 0.1 \\ \hline y' & -0.15 & 0 & 0.27 \\ & \searrow & - & \nearrow \end{array}$$

$\therefore$ $(0, 0)$ is a stationary point (a minimum).

For a minimum, $A' = 0$:

$$\begin{aligned} A' &= \dfrac{\pi}{2}r^2 - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}r \\ &= \dfrac{1}{2}r\left(\pi r - \sqrt{3}\right) = 0 \end{aligned}$$

$$r = 0 \text{ or } \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\pi} \quad (r > 0)$$

$$A'' = \pi r - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$

When $r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\pi}$:

$$A'' = \pi\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\pi}\right) - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} > 0$$

$\therefore$ minimum at $r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\pi}$.
